analysis.title: Antero Midstream Corp. (AM): First Take: 3Q26 Miss on Gathering; Buyback Pace in Focus, Growth Still Partially Gas Price Dependent
key_insights: AM reported 3Q26 adj. EBITDA of $291m, below GSe of $314m (-7.3%) and FactSet consensus of $313m (-7.0%).
The miss vs GSe came from softer Gathering (volumes, margins) and Water (volumes). JV contributions were in line.

Sponsor Antero Resources reported net production of 4.23 bcfe/d vs GSe of 4.27 bcfe/d and cut its 4Q26 production guidance to 4.3 bcfe/d from 4.4-4.5 bcfe/d, citing expected 4Q26 curtailments of 15-20 bcfe.
AM reiterated 2026 EBITDA guidance of $1,190-1,240m (GSe $1,216m, consensus $1,214m). GS says the 3Q miss and 4Q curtailments could move its estimate to the lower end of the range, all else equal.

Adj. FCF after dividends guidance rose to $700-760m from $330-390m on the $377m Veolia litigation proceeds. Excluding the proceeds, guidance is unchanged and the midpoint is in line with GSe of $364m.
3Q26 buybacks were about $27m vs GSe of about $89m, up from $8m in 2Q26. GS expects the call to focus on buyback pace given the Veolia proceeds and soft YTD repurchases.
AM used the roughly $377m Veolia inflow in July to reduce debt. Leverage ended the quarter at 2.8x, down from the low 3x range at 2Q26.

No update on the East Side Express intrastate pipeline (capex $200-300m, phased in service 2028-2029, construction began 2Q26). Nearer-term in-basin drivers are water operations for two AR DUC pads in 4Q26 and about 80 mmcf/d of added compression in the liquids-rich corridor in 4Q26.
GS says curtailments show the AM growth story is still partly gas-price dependent.
GS keeps AM at Neutral with a $24 12-month price target (11x 2027 EBITDA), unchanged, vs a $20.75 price (15.7% upside).

market_movers.rationale: Price target and estimates unchanged after a 3Q26 EBITDA miss. Target is 11x 2027 EBITDA, a roughly 2x discount to GS's gassy midstream group because of the business mix and counterparty concentration (AR is over 90% of revenue).

sector_views.rationale: AM trades at a discount to long-haul gas transmission peers because of its gathering, processing and water focus and high sponsor concentration.

earnings_insights: AM 3Q26 reported adj. EBITDA $291m vs GSe $314m and FactSet consensus $313m, a miss. 2Q26 reported was $289m.
AM 3Q26 reported adj. FCF $178m (ex-Veolia) vs GSe $183m. Capex $45m vs GSe $78m. DPS $0.225, in line.
G&C op income reported $181m vs GSe $202m. LP/HP/Compression volumes were -2%/-5%/-6% vs GSe. LP gathering 4,067 mmcf/d vs GSe 4,162.
Water op income reported $1m (ex-Veolia) vs GSe $8m. Fresh water 89 kb/d vs GSe 105 kb/d (-15%), up 9% QoQ. Well completions 22 vs GSe 20.
JV distributions reported $35m vs GSe $36m. JV processing 1,607 mmcf/d vs GSe 1,600.
FY26 EBITDA guidance reiterated at $1,190-1,240m. GSe FY26E EBITDA $1,215.8m, FY27E $1,314.9m. GSe FY26E EPS $1.09 (estimate).
Antero Resources 3Q26 curtailments were about 10 bcfe vs prior guidance of about 5 bcfe, with 15-20 bcfe expected in 4Q26.
risk_factors: Sponsor Antero Resources is over 90% of revenue, a counterparty concentration risk.
Curtailments and gas-price dependence could weigh on volumes and EBITDA.
Higher capex could reduce capital return opportunities.
Sponsor ownership concentration and corporate governance.
Upside risks: better AR drilling efficiencies, larger capex reductions, stronger in-basin demand growth.

tension_points.bull_case: Leverage is 2.8x with ample balance sheet capacity and liquidity for growth and capital returns, the $377m Veolia proceeds are available, and organic growth options remain (East Side Express, in-basin water and compression additions).
tension_points.bear_case: Buybacks have been softer than expected YTD, and curtailments plus lower AR 4Q26 production guidance show growth is still partly gas-price dependent.
tension_points.what_invalidates: 4Q26 EBITDA coming in below the implied guidance bridge given 15-20 bcfe of curtailments, which could put FY26 at the low end of the $1,190-1,240m range.

theme_stances.key_argument: Curtailments in the quarter and on the 4Q26 outlook remind that AM's growth story is still partly gas-price dependent.
theme_stances.evidence: growth story is still, at least in-part, gas-price dependent
